title: Homologous synapse counts vary less than Poisson sampling in 8 C. elegans and more than Poisson in larval and 3 adult Drosophila connectomes; neuron gains remove half of the fly excess
abstract:
We tested how different the synapse counts of the same connection are in two copies: left and right in one animal, or two animals. The reference is independent Poisson sampling around one common weight. The test conditions on the total count n of each connection pair, so the unknown true weight cancels. The dispersion index phi is the observed variance divided by the Poisson variance. We used 20 comparisons: 8 C. elegans nerve rings (Witvliet et al. 2021), one first-instar larval Drosophila brain, and three adult Drosophila connectomes (FlyWire FAFB v783, male CNS v1.0, BANC v888).

In C. elegans, left and right copies of connections with n of 16 or more had pooled phi = 0.50 (95% bootstrap interval 0.41 to 0.60) in 8 animals; the Poisson null was 1.00 (p = 0.0005). Two animal pairs gave phi = 0.73. Neuron-level gains did not improve held-out predictions. In the larva, left-right phi was about 2 for n from 4 to 63 and did not increase with n. In adult flies, phi increased with n: within one animal, phi for n of 16 or more was 4.1 to 4.6 in all three animals; between animals it was 8.3 to 9.9, and 14 to 17 for n of 64 or more. Input and output gains for each neuron removed 50 to 56% of the excess between animals and 27 to 41% within animals. Input gains removed more excess than output gains in all 9 fly comparisons and gave larger held-out gains.

Main limitations: each species uses a different synapse definition and reconstruction method, so absolute phi values are not a pure biological comparison between species. Fly analyses use only cell types with one neuron per side. Worm data cover only the nerve ring and use human annotation.

display.caption: (A) Dispersion phi of homologous synapse counts against the total count n, with one global scale per comparison; the dotted line is Poisson sampling. Blue: C. elegans (8 animals pooled left versus right, solid; 2 animal pairs, dashed; 95% bootstrap intervals). Orange: larval Drosophila left versus right. Green: adult Drosophila left versus right in three animals. Yellow: adult Drosophila animal versus animal (six comparisons). (B) phi for n of 16 or more with one global scale (filled), with neuron input and output gains (open), and the Poisson null after the gain fit (black bar).

(A) phi after neuron-level input and output gains by count stratum; dotted lines are the Poisson null for the same fit. (B) Edge-specific SD of log(x/y) after gains, for n of 4 or more. C. elegans has SD zero because phi is at most 1.
